en.title: Marvel and WEBTOON Unleash 3 New Vertical Comics at SDCC
en.summary: Get ready for a fresh wave of Marvel heroes and villains in a brand-new format. San Diego Comic-Con unveiled an exciting collaboration bringing iconic characters to the vertical-scroll world of WEBTOON.
en.body:
The vibrant halls of San Diego Comic-Con often serve as a launchpad for major announcements, and this year was no exception for Marvel fans. In a move that bridges the gap between traditional comic book titans and the burgeoning digital webcomic scene, **Marvel** has officially partnered with **WEBTOON**, the world's leading digital comics platform. This collaboration introduces three original series designed specifically for WEBTOON's signature vertical-scroll format, promising a fresh way for fans to experience the Marvel Universe.

The newly announced slate includes titles that playfully hint at the unique blend of characters and platforms. We're getting **Tony's Girl**, which suggests a deep dive into the personal life of a certain genius billionaire. Then there's the wonderfully chaotic **That Time Deadpool Fell Into WEBTOON...and Found The Longest Title of All Time!!!**, an obvious nod to the Merc with a Mouth's penchant for breaking the fourth wall and embracing absurdity. Rounding out the initial offerings is **X-Men Korea**, pointing towards exciting new narratives and perhaps even new characters emerging from a different corner of the globe within the expansive mutant saga.

## A New Dimension for Superheroes

This partnership is more than just a novelty; it represents a strategic expansion for Marvel into a medium that has exploded in popularity, particularly among younger, mobile-first audiences. WEBTOON's vertical-scroll format is inherently suited for on-the-go consumption, allowing readers to effortlessly glide through panels with a flick of their thumb. By tailoring these stories for this format, Marvel is not just adapting existing characters but is likely exploring new narrative structures and visual storytelling techniques that leverage the unique strengths of digital comics. The characters and lore that fans have loved for decades will now be accessible in a format that feels native to the devices they use every day, potentially drawing in a new generation of readers who may not have engaged with traditional comic books.

## What This Means for the Fandom

For the passionate Marvel and WEBTOON communities, this announcement is a cause for celebration and eager anticipation. It signifies a commitment to innovation and a willingness to meet fans where they are. The potential for these new series to explore different facets of the Marvel Universe, perhaps with unique artistic styles and storytelling approaches from WEBTOON creators, is immense. Fans are already buzzing with theories about how characters like Deadpool will adapt to the webcomic format, and what kind of fresh perspectives **X-Men Korea** might bring to the mutant struggle. This collaboration opens up exciting possibilities for character development and story arcs that might not fit as neatly into the established print continuity, offering a playground for creative experimentation that could enrich the overall Marvel tapestry.

## What's Next

While specific release dates for **Tony's Girl**, **That Time Deadpool Fell Into WEBTOON...and Found The Longest Title of All Time!!!**, and **X-Men Korea** have not yet been announced, the reveal at San Diego Comic-Con indicates that development is well underway. Fans should keep a close eye on official Marvel and WEBTOON channels for further updates, including potential previews and launch schedules in the coming months.
